tasks.question: What is the dependency chain from recursive type tagging method calls within the tuple-to-JSON conversion method that could lead to infinite recursion when serializing nested tuples with circular references?
tasks.reference_answer: TagTuple.to_json recursively calls serializer.tag on each item; dispatch returns JSONTag.tag which calls the selected to_json (src/flask/json/tag.py:87-90,133-154,289-295). There is no cycle detection in this tagging traversal. A tuple can participate in an indirect cycle through a list/dict, causing repeated traversal and ordinarily RecursionError at Python recursion depth. Ordinary immutable tuples do not directly contain themselves; deep finite nesting is also depth-limited rather than an infinite cycle.

tasks.question: Where in the serialization pipeline for the JSON tag class that handles Markup API objects are the lower-level helper functions that the conversion method delegates to?
tasks.reference_answer: TagMarkup.check tests whether __html__ is callable; to_json delegates to that method on the value and converts its result with str (src/flask/json/tag.py:181-185). The helper implementation belongs to the object class, not Flask. JSONTag.tag wraps the conversion under the tag key (src/flask/json/tag.py:87-90). The check does not prove the callable accepts zero arguments or cannot raise; errors from protocol invocation are not caught here.

tasks.question: Why does the method that opens application package resources relative to the root path restrict file opening to read-only modes?
tasks.reference_answer: open_resource permits only r, rt and rb and opens relative to root_path (src/flask/app.py:353-361). open_instance_resource explicitly allows writes relative to instance_path (src/flask/app.py:363-368). This API distinction separates reading packaged resources from mutable instance files. It is not a filesystem security boundary and cannot prevent writes through other APIs; stronger immutability claims are not established by this method.

tasks.question: Why does the class that handles UUID serialization in the tagged JSON serialization system enable bidirectional conversion between UUID instances and their hexadecimal string representations?
tasks.reference_answer: TagUUID recognizes UUID instances, serializes value.hex under the " u" tag and reconstructs UUID(value) (src/flask/json/tag.py:191-202). TaggedJSONSerializer tags before dumping and recursively untags after loading (src/flask/json/tag.py:289-327), preserving UUID value/type through JSON. A valid roundtrip check uses u=uuid4(); s.loads(s.dumps(u)) == u, not a second uuid4() call.

tasks.question: Why does the CLI helper class that manages Flask application discovery implement lazy loading through a cached instance attribute rather than during initialization?
tasks.reference_answer: ScriptInfo starts with _loaded_app=None and load_app reuses a cached app (src/flask/cli.py:331-339). FlaskGroup looks up built-in/plugin commands before loading app-defined commands (src/flask/cli.py:609-634), permitting discovery when app loading fails. However, help command listing does attempt to load the app and catches failures while retaining built-ins (src/flask/cli.py:636-655). Lazy loading provides controlled timing and reuse; it does not mean every help request avoids imports.
